newsitem.title: INDIA: India welcomes U.S. extradition of Sikh suspect.
newsitem.headline: India welcomes U.S. extradition of Sikh suspect.

text.p: India praised the United States on Friday for extraditing a suspected top Sikh militant leader wanted by New Delhi in connection with attempted assassination and kidnapping.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Daya Singh Lahoria was extradited by the United States on Thursday and was expected to arrive in India in a day or two, after a stopover in London, to face charges.
"This is a very important event," the spokesman said. "We are quite pleased with the response of the U.S. government."
Earlier this month a Texas court cleared the way for the extradition of Lahoria, who was arrested in Minneapolis in 1995.

Lahoria, also known as Sandhu, is believed to be one of the leaders of the Khalistan Liberation Force, a militant outfit fighting for a separate Sikh nation in the northern state of Punjab which it calls Khalistan, or Land of the Pure.

The Central Bureau of Investigation, India's federal police agency, said Lahoria was wanted for the attempted assassination in September 1993 of the then head of the Congress party's youth wing, M.S. Bitta.
He is also suspected of involvement in the abduction of the son of former government minister Ram Niwas Mirdha, as well as arms trafficking in India, authorities said.
Lahoria was arrested by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service (INS) in August 1995 at the Minneapolis-St. Paul airport and charged with illegal entry into the United States and visa fraud.
His wife Suman Sood, who was arrested with him, has also been extradited.
Indian officials said it was the first time the United States had extradited those accused under Indian law.
"It is a very good signal that these kinds of activities are under scrutiny," the Foreign Ministry spokesman said, noting that a bilateral extradition treaty was almost complete.
